extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) is a benchmark for text embeddings that spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.citeAs: Muennighoff, N., Tazi, N., Magne, L., & Reimers, N. (2023). MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv preprint arXiv:2210.07316v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) consists of 58 datasets covering 112 languages from 8 embedding tasks: Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MTEB incorporates SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR alongside a variety of other datasets from various tasks to provide a holistic performance review of text embedding models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are typically binary variables denoting duplicate or paraphrase pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Considerations related to the process of converting the "raw" annotations into the final labels (e.g., uncertainty, disagreement analysis).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard at https://github.com/embeddings-benchm/mteb .
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and thus serves as the gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: No single best solution, with different models dominating different tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Long document datasets are still missing. The longest datasets in MTEB have a few hundred words. Task imbalance: Tasks in MTEB have a different amount of datasets with summarization consisting of only a single dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB tasks include Classification, Clustering, Pair Classification, Reranking, Retrieval, Semantic Textual Similarity (STS), and Summarization.
